confidence.rationale: The formulation matches authoritative CBT descriptions, but a teaching model is not itself proof of every causal arrow.

limitations: Not every emotion requires a conscious inference, not every distressing interpretation is inaccurate, and changing a thought does not guarantee emotional change.

scope.population: People described using a cognitive-behavioral formulation.
scope.temporal_scope: Situation-level response and repeated maintenance cycles.

claims.statement: The CBT cognitive model treats interpretation of a situation as related to emotional, behavioral, and often physiological responses, while contemporary formulation also considers reciprocal behavioral and contextual feedback.

confidence.rationale: The cycle integrates established component relationships and clinical formulation, but its edges and dominant direction must be tested for the particular problem and context.

claims.falsifiable_boundary: The proposed network is challenged when changing its nominated process does not alter downstream outcomes or when alternative contextual, social, physiological, or learning models explain the pattern better.
limitations: A generic cycle should not be presented as the explanation for a person before individualized assessment and competing hypotheses.

boundary_conditions: A concrete target problem, measurable responses, declared goals, and repeated observations before and after intervention.
scope.population: Individuals or explicitly defined groups receiving cognitive-behavioral formulation.

claims.statement: For a specified person and context, interpretations, emotional and physiological responses, coping behavior, consequences, and beliefs may form a self-maintaining reciprocal network with multiple possible intervention points.
claims.temporal_ordering: Situation, interpretation, response, behavior, and consequences are repeatedly time-indexed; feedback to later expectations is assessed in subsequent episodes.

causal_assumptions.consistency: CBT and comparator versions differ across trials and require stratified interpretation.
causal_assumptions.exchangeability: Randomization supports baseline exchangeability within trials; attrition and bias can compromise it.
causal_assumptions.interference: Participant-level interference is generally assumed but group and therapist effects may occur.
causal_assumptions.positivity: Included trials enrolled participants eligible for compared conditions.

claims.causal_estimand: Average effect of assignment to protocol-defined CBT versus the declared control condition on post-treatment depressive symptom severity in the included randomized trials.

confidence.rationale: A very large meta-analysis of randomized comparisons found a moderate-to-large pooled effect versus controls, while heterogeneity and comparator choice limit one universal estimate.

estimate.metric: Hedges g for CBT versus control conditions
estimate.notes: Negative direction denotes lower depressive symptom severity; the source reports g = 0.79 in magnitude favoring CBT.

limitations: Treatment efficacy does not identify cognitive change as the unique mediator, prove the full cognitive model, or establish superiority over every other psychotherapy.

boundary_conditions: Protocol-defined CBT, depression target, trial comparator, treatment format, and risk-of-bias conditions represented in the synthesis.
scope.population: Patients represented in randomized CBT trials for depression.

claims.statement: Across randomized depression trials synthesized by Cuijpers and colleagues, protocol-defined CBT reduced depressive symptoms more than control conditions on average, with effects dependent on comparator and study quality.
claims.temporal_ordering: Treatment assignment precedes post-treatment symptom measurement.

confidence.rationale: Nested randomized studies support cognitive variables as candidate mediators, but many designs do not establish temporal or causal mediation and cognitive measures vary.

indirect_effect.notes: Cognitive variables were most commonly assessed; negative thinking had the strongest support for adult depression prevention.

limitations: Statistical mediation does not prove that changing a particular thought caused symptom improvement or that cognition is the only pathway.

scope.population: Participants in psychological and psychoeducational prevention trials included in the review.
scope.temporal_scope: Intervention, candidate mediator assessment, and later symptom outcome as reported in included studies.

claims.statement: In a systematic review of prevention trials, measured cognitive change statistically mediated some depression and anxiety outcomes, but constructs, interventions, and mediation methods were heterogeneous.
claims.temporal_ordering: Ordering varied across included mediator studies and was not uniformly sufficient for causal mediation.

confidence.rationale: This follows from the distinction between intervention efficacy, component effects, statistical mediation, and causal mechanism identification.

limitations: Specific well-designed component and mediation experiments may provide stronger mechanism evidence, but must be evaluated separately.
claims.statement: Evidence that a CBT package improves an outcome establishes a treatment effect within scope, not that every component worked or that one cognitive mechanism uniquely produced the benefit.

evidence.design: Random-effects meta-analysis of randomized CBT comparisons for depression.

effect.notes: Magnitude favored CBT; sign is represented as lower symptom severity.

evidence.extraction_locator: PubMed abstract reporting 409 trials, 52,702 patients, control comparison, follow-up, and sensitivity analyses.
limitations: Trials varied in CBT type, control, population, delivery, quality, and follow-up; superiority over other psychotherapies was small and not robust in sensitivity analyses.
evidence.summary: CBT showed moderate-to-large average benefit over control conditions, with significant effects at follow-up and important comparator and sensitivity qualifications.

evidence.design: Systematic review of candidate mediators in psychological and psychoeducational depression and anxiety prevention trials.
evidence.extraction_locator: Systematic-review abstract and results covering 28 mediator studies nested in randomized trials with 7,442 participants.
limitations: Interventions were broader than CBT alone, mediator timing and constructs varied, and statistical mediation often fell short of causal identification.
evidence.summary: Cognitive variables, especially negative thinking in adults, showed the strongest mediator support, while mechanism research remained limited and heterogeneous.

evidence.design: Mechanism-focused interpretation of mediator studies nested in randomized prevention trials.
evidence.extraction_locator: Review conclusions that mechanism research remains limited despite candidate cognitive, behavioral, emotional, and interpersonal mediators.
limitations: The source reviews prevention interventions rather than individualized reciprocal CBT networks and cannot validate every edge in the proposed cycle.
evidence.summary: Candidate processes were observed, but the review does not establish one complete or unique cognitive-behavioral maintenance mechanism.

metadata.description: Separates situation, interpretation, emotion, physiology, behavior, consequences, beliefs, CBT techniques, treatment effects, and proposed mechanisms of change.
metadata.title: Evidence pack for cognitive-behavioral formulation

boundary_notes: The model does not require every emotion to be preceded by a conscious verbal thought.
Thoughts, emotions, physiology, behavior, and context can influence one another; a simple one-way diagram is a teaching aid rather than a complete causal model.
A useful formulation for one person is not automatically a population-level scientific law.
objects.definition: Clinical formulation framework in which a person's interpretation of a situation is related to emotional, physiological, and behavioral responses, while behavior and consequences can feed back into later interpretations and beliefs.
objects.label: CBT cognitive model

objects.definition: External event, internal sensation, memory, image, or anticipation that becomes relevant to a person's current goals, needs, or concerns.
objects.label: Personally significant situation
objects.scope: A formulation specifies the concrete situation rather than treating all distress as one context.

boundary_notes: A reported thought is one measurement of interpretation and may be reconstructed after the emotional episode.
objects.definition: Verbal, imaginal, or nonverbal meaning assigned to a situation, which may be rapid, automatic, partly conscious, or deliberately considered.
objects.label: Situational interpretation

objects.definition: Time-indexed subjective emotional experience occurring in relation to the personally significant situation.
objects.label: Emotional response

boundary_notes: Physiology is not interchangeable with subjective emotion or interpretation.
objects.definition: Time-indexed autonomic, endocrine, muscular, respiratory, or other bodily response during the episode.
objects.label: Physiological response

objects.definition: Observable action, omission, communication, safety behavior, approach, or avoidance occurring during or after the episode.
objects.function_note: The same action can have different short- and long-term functions in different contexts.
objects.label: Coping or avoidance behavior
objects.response_topography: Situation-specific approach, avoidance, reassurance, withdrawal, problem solving, or other observable response.

boundary_notes: Immediate relief can coexist with longer-term maintenance of a problem.
objects.definition: Immediate and delayed changes in distress, safety, task completion, social response, learning opportunity, or valued functioning following behavior.
objects.label: Short- and long-term consequences

boundary_notes: A belief is not directly observed and should not be inferred solely because a therapist's formulation seems plausible.
objects.definition: More general assumptions, rules, self-representations, and predictions that organize interpretation across situations.
objects.label: Beliefs and future expectations

boundary_notes: Different questionnaires and cognitive constructs are not interchangeable mediators.
objects.definition: Measured pattern of negative interpretations, expectations, or self-referential cognitions studied as a possible mediator of intervention outcomes.
objects.label: Negative thinking process

boundary_notes: The complete cycle is a formulation hypothesis, not a single universally established mechanism.
objects.definition: Proposed context-dependent process in which interpretations, emotions, physiology, behavior, consequences, and beliefs reciprocally constrain future responding.
objects.label: Reciprocal cognitive-behavioral maintenance cycle
realization_conditions: The formulation specifies a recurring situation and measurable responses for one person or a declared population.
At least one feedback path is temporally observed or experimentally manipulated.
Competing biological, social, learning, and contextual explanations remain testable.

boundary_notes: Valid thoughts may call for problem solving, acceptance, protection, or environmental change rather than disputation.
objects.definition: Structured examination of an interpretation or prediction using evidence, alternative explanations, decentering, or Socratic questions.
objects.delivery: Guided or self-directed evaluation using a treatment protocol appropriate to the problem.
objects.label: Cognitive evaluation practice

objects.definition: Planned real-world or simulated action used to test a concrete prediction and collect new observable information.
objects.delivery: Specify a prediction, safe action, observable result, and review of what was learned.
objects.label: Behavioral experiment

boundary_notes: CBT is an umbrella family; efficacy estimates depend on target condition, components, comparator, format, provider, and risk of bias.
objects.definition: Structured psychological treatment combining cognitive and behavioral methods according to a declared manual, formulation, dose, provider, and target condition.
objects.delivery: Qualified guided treatment or declared self-help protocol with specified sessions, components, and comparison condition.
objects.label: Protocol-defined cognitive behavior therapy

objects.definition: Clinical or research context in which adults with depressive symptoms or disorders receive CBT or a comparison condition.

dimensions.comparator: control psychotherapy pharmacotherapy or combined care

objects.label: Adult depression treatment context
objects.scope: Trials included in the declared depression treatment synthesis.

objects.definition: Protocol-defined severity of depressive symptoms after treatment or at follow-up.
objects.label: Depressive symptom severity

objects.definition: Validated self-report or clinician-rated scale used to quantify depressive symptom severity at declared time points.
objects.label: Depression symptom scale
objects.method: Administer and score a declared validated depression measure according to protocol.
